A person’s writing style can change over time, and it can also shift across genres or text types. One study finds that temporal drift is a strong factor in authorship verification, with performance worsening as the time gap between documents grows, and that stylistic features can matter differently across genre transitions [2]. Another study on scientific prose reports substantial post-2022 changes in vocabulary, punctuation, readability, and syntax, showing that writing trajectories can change in rate and direction over time [4].

Across text types, style is also shaped by genre and rewriting. One paper finds genre exerts a stronger influence on stylistic features than the source itself, while model differences matter too [5]. Other studies show that rewriting or personalization can move text toward a more normalized or hybrid style, often reducing markers of individual voice but not fully eliminating them [1, 3, 8, 10].
